section_summary.extract_value: This Discussion section presents findings from a single study examining relationships between interoceptive awareness (IA) dimensions measured by the MAIA and multiple facets of body image in a community sample of adult men and women. The study found that specific MAIA subscales (particularly Trusting, Attention Regulation, and Self-Regulation) were significant predictors of positive body image facets, while the Noticing subscale showed unexpected negative associations with body appreciation. The authors note this is the first evidence of relationships between interoceptive facets and functionality appreciation and body pride, and discuss important clinical implications for eating disorder interventions.
